correctness.rationale: For m>=2 uniform iid coupons, conditioning on first repeat B=t<=m leaves m-t+1 unseen types, and future coupon discoveries have independent geometric waiting times with parameters j/m. The endpoint B=m+1 implies C=m. Adjacent conditional laws couple with difference G_{m-t+1,m}-1>=0 (last endpoint separately), establishing strictly decreasing stochastic regression and negative quadrant dependence for all increasing tails. The exact birthday probability and harmonic conditional mean give covariance as a finite sum. With B/sqrt(m) Rayleigh and uniform exponential tails, the conditional mean difference D_m(B)=sum_{j=1}^{B-2} j/(m-j) is asymptotic B^2/(2m), and uniform integrability controls rare large B. Rayleigh moments E[R],E[R^2],E[R^3] yield Cov(B,C)/sqrt(m)->-sqrt(pi/8). Using Var(B)/m->(4-pi)/2 and Var(C)/m^2->pi^2/6 gives m Corr(B,C)->-sqrt(3/(2pi(4-pi))). All claimed exceptional and normalization cases are handled.
residual_risks: The asymptotic moment exchange requires the proof’s exponential birthday tail and separate high-B error estimate; finite checks cannot establish the limit.
The assertion about covariance of increasing unbounded transforms assumes the required product moment exists, as stated.

value.rationale: The first repeat and final coverage times are canonical linked stopping times, yet their joint negative regression is not determined by their well-known marginals. A sharp mixed covariance and correlation law characterizes a natural stochastic dependence scale and is meaningful independently of an overarching theorem.
residual_risks: The leading negative covariance may be recoverable from an uninspected classical joint occupancy result; the value rests on conditional order and explicit sharp constants as a combined theorem.
